kk_runs.detail: Four distinct fixed exponents 11/22/33/44, nonempty prologue and payload literals; honest run exists with all four operations succeeding and matching crossed keys. Symbolic term algebra and synthetic literals; no computational crypto, native primitive, freshness or private-payload secrecy claim.

handshake_agrees.detail: Concrete symbolic suite satisfies the corrected Good contract; kk_runs supplies both payload-domain premises (True for symbolic terms) and proves the four DH calls succeed for fixed parties/ephemerals. HKDF/hash domains establish valid keys and associated data internally. Symbolic term algebra and synthetic literals; no native primitive correctness, freshness or private-payload secrecy claim.

kk_secret.detail: Construct a successful concrete transcript and sent1 reconstruction, then apply kk_secret. Attacker knows all other names and all public keys. Symbolic term algebra and synthetic literals; no computational crypto, native primitive, freshness or private-payload secrecy claim.

kk_secret_init.detail: Concrete successful sent1/read2 and secret-name membership premises are discharged through kk_secret, which applies kk_secret_init. Symbolic term algebra and synthetic literals; no computational crypto, native primitive, freshness or private-payload secrecy claim.

kk_secret_resp.detail: Concrete successful read1/write2 and both static-secret premises are discharged through kk_secret, which applies kk_secret_resp. Symbolic term algebra and synthetic literals; no computational crypto, native primitive, freshness or private-payload secrecy claim.

kk_secret_init_tight.detail: Negative control on the same successful handshake: expose initiator static 11 AND ephemeral 33 while responder 22/44 stay secret; attacker derives both initiator transport keys. Symbolic term algebra and synthetic literals; no computational crypto, native primitive, freshness or private-payload secrecy claim.

kk_forward_secret.detail: Prove concrete statics differ from both ephemerals; successful transcript remains secret after deriving both static secrets and both messages. Four transport key non-derivability conclusions. Symbolic term algebra and synthetic literals; no computational crypto, native primitive, freshness or private-payload secrecy claim.

kk_authentic.detail: Concrete transcript; O is every honest call but responder 22 answering this message 1. Under it the attacker still derives message 1 (initiator 11's request) and 22's answer to another session (ephemerals 55/66), which that session's initiator accepts; the no-answer premise holds by construction and every attacker and secrecy premise is discharged; this initiator then rejects every term the attacker derives. Under AllCalls the honest reply is derivable and accepted, so O does the work. Symbolic term algebra and synthetic literals; no computational crypto, native primitive, freshness or private-payload secrecy claim.

kk_authentic_resp.detail: Concrete transcript; O is every honest call but initiator 11 writing 22 a message 1 with payload1. Under it 11's request with a different payload (decided unequal) is derivable and 22 accepts it; both static-secret and attacker premises are discharged; 22 then accepts no derivable message 1 as from 11 with payload1. Under AllCalls the honest message 1 is derivable and accepted. Symbolic term algebra and synthetic literals; no computational crypto, native primitive, freshness or private-payload secrecy claim.

kk_agree.detail: Concrete transcript; O is exactly the run's two logged calls (11's request, 22's answer). The reply is derived through both, accepted, and kk_agree returns the logged call by 22 answering this message 1 with matching sessions. Symbolic term algebra and synthetic literals; no computational crypto, native primitive, freshness or private-payload secrecy claim.

kk_agree_resp.detail: Concrete transcript; O is exactly the run's two logged calls. Message 1 is derived through 11's logged request and accepted, and kk_agree_resp returns that logged call with ephemeral 33 and the written state. Symbolic term algebra and synthetic literals; no computational crypto, native primitive, freshness or private-payload secrecy claim.

kk_authentic_tight.detail: Negative control on the same successful handshake: responder static 22 leaked (11/33/44 secret), O barred from every answer by 22. The attacker has 11 send message 1, picks its own name 55 and writes a message 2 that this initiator accepts, so kk_authentic fails when its responder-secrecy premise does. Symbolic term algebra and synthetic literals; no computational crypto, native primitive, freshness or private-payload secrecy claim.

kk_authentic_resp_tight.detail: Negative control (key-compromise impersonation): responder static 22 leaked, O barred from every request by 11. The attacker writes, with its own ephemeral 55, a message 1 that 22 accepts as from 11 with payload1, so kk_authentic_resp fails when its responder-secrecy premise does. Symbolic term algebra and synthetic literals; no computational crypto, native primitive, freshness or private-payload secrecy claim.
